extracted.intended_audience: Reporters, editors, photographers and all members of the news staff of the New York Times
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for New York Times newsroom staff on ethical behavior, conflicts of interest, accuracy, and photojournalism practices to protect the newspaper's authority and readers' trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect the integrity and authority of the newspaper
rubrics_metrics.description: Our greatest strength is the authority and reputation of the Times. We must do nothing that would undermine or dilute it and everything possible to enhance it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff should prioritize actions that protect and enhance the paper's reputation; this is presented as an overarching principle guiding all conduct and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain highest possible standards to preserve readers' faith
rubrics_metrics.description: At a time of growing public suspicion about impartiality, accuracy and integrity, the Times and its staff must maintain the highest possible standards to ensure we do nothing that might erode readers’ faith and confidence in our news columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This general standard requires vigilance in daily journalism practice to avoid activities or errors that would undermine public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid actual or apparent conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff members should be vigilant in avoiding any activity that might pose an actual or apparent conflict of interest and thus threaten the newspaper’s ethical standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to outside activities, relationships, and any behavior that could create the appearance of compromised impartiality; vigilance is required even for apparent conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice journalism beyond reproach
rubrics_metrics.description: The journalism we practice daily must be beyond reproach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad exhortation implying strict adherence to accuracy, fairness, independence, and ethical norms in reporting and editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No falsification of news reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Falsifying any part of a news report cannot be tolerated and will result automatically in disciplinary action up to and including termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zero-tolerance rule: any fabrication, invention, or deliberate misrepresentation in reporting triggers automatic disciplinary measures, up to firing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images must be genuine in every way
rubrics_metrics.description: Images in our pages that purport to depict reality must be genuine in every way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable to photographs and other pictorial representations used in news coverage — they must accurately represent the depicted reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not add, rearrange, reverse, distort, or remove elements in a scene (cropping excepted)
rubrics_metrics.description: No people or objects may be added, rearranged, reversed, distorted or removed from a scene (except for the recognized practice of cropping to omit extraneous outer portions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital or physical manipulation that changes the content or meaning of an image is prohibited; cropping to remove extraneous outer portions is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit color and gray-scale adjustments to minimal necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments of color or gray scale should be limited to those minimally necessary for clear and accurate reproduction, analogous to the 'burning' and 'dodging' that formerly took place in darkroom processing of images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical edits are permitted only when essential for faithful reproduction; excessive retouching is disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictures of news situations must not be posed
rubrics_metrics.description: Pictures of news situations must not be posed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staged poses that manufacture or alter the reality of a news event are forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly disclose any constructed or contrived images
rubrics_metrics.description: In the cases of collages, montages, portraits, fashion or home design illustrations, fanciful contrived situations and demonstrations of how a device is used, our intervention should be unmistakable to the reader, and unmistakably free of intent to deceive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When images are constructed or illustrative rather than documentary, the reader must be made clearly aware of the intervention; intent to deceive must be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use captions and credits to acknowledge intervention when doubt exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions and credits should further acknowledge our intervention if the slightest doubt is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When any manipulation, staging, or other intervention could be questioned, the caption/credit must plainly state the nature of the intervention to avoid confusion or deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult editors on doubtful photographic cases or exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The design director, a masthead editor or the news desk should be consulted on doubtful cases or proposals for exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If staff are uncertain whether an image or proposed exception conforms to policy, they must seek guidance from senior editors or the design director before publication.
